transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-28
Start: 16:00 PDT
Duration: 42 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jules Moreno (Redwood SE), Nina Cho (OpalWave CTO), Marcus Li (OpalWave Platform), Etta Ramos (OpalWave Product)

Auto-generated summary: quick discovery on PLG sprint credits and connectivity. Customer evaluating quick time-to-first-token but has enterprise constraints.

[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for doing this, I'll kick off, uh, quick intro from our side, I'm Samir, AE at Redwood Inference, with me is Jules our solutions engineer
[00:08] Jules: hi all, hello, nice to meet you, i'll field the deeper infra and perf questions
[00:12] Nina: thanks, yeah Nina here, CTO, quick intro: we're OpalWave, mid-stage API platform, building contextual help and search over docs, experimenting with embeddings + chat, looking for fastest path to a prototype for our PLG funnel
[00:24] Etta: and I'm Etta, PM for the search product, main success metric is conversion lift within two weeks of prototype, so TTFT is pretty important
[00:33] Marcus: Marcus here, platform, i'll be the one looking at VPC, infra and security, we need to make sure any hosted flow can be locked down or we have a private option
[00:41] Samir: great. quick agenda: clarify goals, current stack, constraints, then TTFT options: self-serve hosted credits, Dedicated reserved, or Private VPC/on-prem, finish with open questions and next steps
[00:56] Nina: sounds good

---

[01:12] Samir: can you walk us through current infra? what's the auth flow, where do requests originate, that sort of thing
[01:20] Marcus: sure, we run services across GCP in us-central1, public APIs fronted by our gateway, product teams will call a microservice to enrich responses, currently we use Vertex for small experiments but it's been clunky on costs. we want an API that the product teams can hit quickly without infra dependency for first prototype
[01:38] Jules: ok that's helpful. for time-to-first-token, our hosted API typically gets teams live in under a day given free credits — you sign up, we give you sandbox credits, and you can make calls. For more secure flows we have VPC peering and Private control plane where you can keep traffic in your VPC
[01:58] Nina: when you say sandbox credits — how big are they? and is there any gating? we worry about runaway costs from some of our early experiments
[02:08] Samir: typical PLG pack is 50k tokens for prototyping, but we can flex. it's designed so you can demo the product and get concrete numbers to justify reserved capacity if you go that route. billing caps and quotas can be set on the account so you don't have runaway spend
[02:26] Etta: 50k tokens — that's reasonable. if we do a quick funnel test with a small subset, how quickly can we go from signup to the first successful inference? like, minutes? hours?
[02:36] Jules: usually minutes. sign up, create an API key, curl into the endpoint. we have quickstart examples and an SDK. if you want to preserve customer PII, you can route through VPC or use our hosted with no retention — we can discuss retention settings in the security pack
[02:52] Marcus: okay retention settings — what's default for hosted? do you persist logs or request payloads? we need to align with our compliance team
[02:58] Samir: by default hosted retains minimal logs for troubleshooting and billing; we have options: no retention in hosted for enterprise customers, and on dedicated/private you control logs and can integrate KMS for encryption at rest
[03:11] Nina: we're SOC 2 aligned and require vendor SOC 2 as well; do you have that? and SSO?
[03:17] Jules: yes, Redwood has SOC 2 Type II attestation, we support SAML/SSO for orgs and RBAC. we'll share the security pack after the call (Samir will put the link in the follow-up)
[03:28] [crosstalk] Marcus: mm-hmm okay that's helpful

[03:40] Samir: moving into hosting fit: small prototype — hosted is fastest and cheapest up front. dedicated is for predictable throughput and isolation; private/VPC is for strict network controls or regulated data
[03:56] Etta: can you quantify expected latency and cost tradeoffs? product cares about snappy responses
[04:03] Jules: sure — for a medium 1k token completion on our hosted multi-tenant endpoints you'd see p50 around 220-300ms depending on model and prompt. dedicated can shave that down if you pin model and get better batching. cost-wise, multi-tenant hosted lowers cost via pooling; dedicated raises cost but gives predictable tail latency
[04:26] Marcus: when you say model, is this redwood-hosted open models or vendor models? can we bring our own weights or use a quantized profile?
[04:35] Jules: we have a curated model catalog including popular open models and quantized variants. customers can request private model onboarding with a process; bring-your-own-model is supported in private/dedicated setups but needs more ops work
[04:46] Nina: ok noted. for our short experiment we probably will start hosted then if numbers look good we might move to a dedicated pilot

---

[05:05] Samir: i want to get into specifics for the pilot. what does success look like? Etta you mentioned conversion lift within two weeks — any specific throughput or latency SLOs to hit?
[05:16] Etta: ideally p50 < 400ms for the enrich call, p90 < 900ms, and prototype must handle 50 RPS burst for demo traffic. accuracy/quality is a product metric we'll monitor but we can define test prompts
[05:30] Jules: that's doable with hosted for a small pilot. we'll validate with a micro-benchmark. for 50 RPS bursts we might need to look at burst capacity or a short dedicated pool for demo windows — we can simulate with our load harness
[05:43] Marcus: load harness sounds good. for connectivity — if we keep hosted, can we restrict calls from our network only? we don't want open keys in demos
[05:52] Samir: yes, we support IP allowlists for API keys, and for tighter control VPC peering with private endpoints is recommended. VPC requires some networking steps (peering or private endpoints) that Jules can walk through in the tech deep dive
[06:06] Jules: quick note — VPC peering for Redwood Private uses customer-managed routing; we recommend setting up a transit gateway in some setups. also for on-prem we have an appliance-like package but that's heavier lift

[06:20] Nina: can you give a sense of how much lead time for VPC peering or private deployment? we have a security review window of two weeks before next product demo
[06:29] Jules: VPC peering typically takes 2-5 business days once networking configs are approved. Private control plane or on-prem could be 4-8 weeks depending on approvals and infra availability. For your two-week window, hosted with IP allowlist plus SOC2 docs is the practical path
[06:44] Etta: ok so hosted for immediate demo, then evaluate dedicated or private after numbers — makes sense

[06:54] Samir: budget question — are you expecting to convert to reserved capacity if the prototype shows good signal? or keep hosted pay-as-you-go?
[07:02] Nina: if we see conversion lift and reasonable unit costs, we prefer predictable monthly committed for budgeting — but need numbers to justify commit
[07:10] Samir: understood. that's exactly what pilot credits are for — get real usage numbers, then we can model dedicated sizing and committed price

---

[07:25] Marcus: security follow-ups — KMS integration for encryption, how do keys work? do you manage keys or can we bring our own?
[07:33] Jules: there are two patterns: Redwood-managed KMS for hosted or customer-managed keys (CMK) via cloud KMS or HSM in Private/Dedicated. For hosted we also offer envelope encryption integrations if you need to bring keys into the loop. we'll include details in the security pack
[07:49] Marcus: and audit logs / SIEM integration? we want to push logs into Splunk for request-level audit
[07:55] Jules: yes, we support audit log exports and syslog/S3 sinks; in private setups you control the log path. hosted can push structured logs to your retention endpoint with appropriate filters

[08:10] Nina: any notable gotchas with prompt context length and KV cache? we do a lot of context enrichment and might hit long chats
[08:18] Jules: we have token limits per model — for huge contexts we recommend chunking and embeddings-based retrieval. also our runtime supports KV caching and prefix caching; sometimes transcripts show 'kay vee cash' in auto-transcripts, so apologies for the transcription quirk, but the tech works as you'd expect
[08:36] Etta: heh noted. what about streaming? we need progressive render in the UI
[08:40] Jules: streaming is supported by the API; you can stream partial tokens to render faster. it's standard in our SDKs

---

[08:50] Samir: let's talk deliverables from this call. Jules will run a small benchmark using your sample prompts; Samir will allocate an initial credit pack and share pricing—Marcus will supply payload examples and desired RPS windows
[09:04] Marcus: yes I'll drop the sample JSONs and a short doc on traffic patterns by Monday
[09:10] Samir: perfect. we'll follow up with security packet (SOC2, SSO guide, KMS options), pricing + pilot terms, and a calendar invite for the VPC deep dive
[09:20] Nina: thanks, what about a simple demo app? do you have a hosted demo we can fork?
[09:25] Jules: we have a demo repo and quickstart with Next.js + serverless examples; I'll paste links in the follow up. it's a small app you can drop in and replace the endpoint with your key
[09:34] Etta: that should speed things, yes

---

[09:40] Speaker 3: (unlabeled) can we talk about estimated costs — rough ballpark for 50k tokens and 1k token completions at 50 RPS?
[09:47] Jules: rough quick math: 50k tokens for prompt+completion covers many demos; per-call cost depends on model size — we will run the benchmark and produce a cost table; Samir will include a per-token estimate in the follow-up. hosted multi-tenant gives best unit economics for prototyping
[10:05] Marcus: good, we'll need the numbers for finance approval

---

[10:12] Samir: any other questions from the product or platform side?
[10:15] Nina: just one — do you do canary rollouts or A/B on model versions? we want to test quality regressions quickly
[10:22] Jules: yes we support rollouts, canary and A/B testing per route. Redwood Optimize can suggest quantization profiles and batching to balance cost/quality and set alerts on regressions tied to prompt sets
[10:36] Nina: ok that's actually useful

[10:40] Samir: last housekeeping: i'll create a Trello/card with the action items and share the benchmark spreadsheet template. we'll tentatively aim to have the benchmark results and pilot terms by 2026-06-04
[10:52] Marcus: works for me
[10:54] Etta: same

[10:57] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the pack and links. quick recap in the thread: (1) hosted quickstart with 50k token credits to prove TTFT and conversion lift, (2) Jules runs perf/cost benchmark with your prompts, (3) Marcus sends payloads/settings, (4) schedule VPC deep dive if needed.
[11:18] Nina: great, appreciate it, bye
[11:20] Samir: thanks all, bye
